about: Every source the page cites, with the date read and the words it supports. An evidence item on the page names one of these ids.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 3: model entry and validation
sources.supports: The checks before analysis. They find undefined symbols, units that disagree, conditions that are not there and open constitutive laws. They also check temperatures, domains, zero scales and dependent inputs.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 4: Dimensionless Number Finder
sources.supports: The dimension matrix, the exact rank, the kernel basis and the n − r groups. Also the repeating variables and the checks of the basis.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 5: worked Buckingham Pi calculation
sources.supports: The variables h, k, ρ, μ, c_p, U and L, with the matrix D, det D_R = −1 and rank 4. The groups hL/k, μ/(ρUL) and ρc_pUL/k, and the familiar basis Nu, Re, Pr.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 6: Model Nondimensionalizer
sources.supports: Scales with their mechanisms and competing scales, nonzero scales, dimensionless variables and their inverses, derivative transformations, substitution into every equation and condition, the common factor, the remaining parameters, the comparison with the Pi basis and the reverse substitution.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 7: worked slab nondimensionalization
sources.supports: The slab equation, its symmetry, convection and initial conditions, and the variables X, τ = Fo and θ.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 8: mathematical regime determination
sources.supports: Dominant balance with complete terms and their scales, reduced equations, supporting inequalities, residuals and balance crossovers. Asymptotic analysis with a declared limit path, the equations of each order, solvability, inner regions and matching, and the difference between a formal expansion, an estimated remainder and a proved bound.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 9: Regime Map Builder
sources.supports: 1D diagrams and 2D slices with chosen axes and fixed parameters, linear and logarithmic axes, layers, the five boundary types with their criteria, unresolved regions, the inspection of a point or a boundary, and limit paths.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 10: heat-transfer definitions and the straight fin
sources.supports: The group definitions with their reference quantities, such as Nu, Bi, Fo, Re and Pr. The fin variables with rank 3 and 4 groups.

sources.title: Specification 6, section 11: initial acceptance suite
sources.supports: Anchor test 1, transient slab conduction: the hand derivation, the dimensionless conditions, the reference temperature solution and the approximation error map.

sources.title: R. J. Ribando, Transient analytical solutions: the plane wall (heat-transfer spreadsheets)
sources.supports: The separation-of-variables solution for transient conduction in a slab (plane wall) with convection at the surfaces (Newton's law of cooling) and a symmetry condition at the centre line, as functions of the Biot and Fourier numbers. The page says that the solutions for the infinite cylinder and the sphere are "even messier" and that its workbook solves their characteristic equations.

sources.title: MIT 2.25 Advanced Fluid Mechanics (Fall 2013): The Buckingham Pi Theorem in Dimensional Analysis
sources.supports: A set of n − r independent Pi groups, with r the rank (the note writes k for it). The note says: "this set of non-dimensional parameters is not unique. They are however independent and form a complete set." It also asks "can I vary all of these variables independently", and it says "Compare with experimental data!"

sources.title: COMSOL 6.3 Heat Transfer Module: Defining the Heat Transfer Coefficients
sources.supports: Nu_L = hL/k, Re_L = ρUL/μ, Pr = μC_p/k, Ra_L = Gr_L Pr, with L the characteristic length.

sources.title: MIT 16 Unified Engineering, thermodynamics notes, section 18.2: Heat Transfer From a Fin
sources.supports: m²L² = hPL²/(kA), the insulated-tip profile cosh(mL(1 − ξ))/cosh(mL) and the base heat flow Q̇/(√(kAhP)(T₀ − T∞)) = tanh(mL).

sources.title: MathJax documentation: MathJax Font Support
sources.supports: The font name mathjax-fira selects a version of the Fira and Fira-Math fonts in MathJax 4.
